question: Who became the first Swiss chemist to win the Nobel Prize in 1913 for his work on the linkage of atoms and the coordination theory?
solution:
The correct answer is **'Alfred Werner**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alfred Werner** won the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1913** for linking atoms in molecules (inorganic chemistry).

 
 
• Alfred Werner was the **first 'inorganic chemist' to win the Nobel Prize.**
 
• Famous research of Alfred Werner:
 
 
• **Coordination Chemistry**
 
• **Nature of Valence**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Walter Heitler** was a German physicist who contributed to '**quantum field theory**' and '**quantum electrodynamics'**.

 
 
• Walter was awarded Max Planck Medal and Marcel Benoist Prize but **never won the Nobel Prize**.
 
 
 
• **Charles Friedel** was a professor of chemistry and mineralogy at the Sorbonne.
 
 
• He is known for his work with James Crafts in 1877 on the **Friedel-Crafts alkylation** and acylation reactions.
 
• He was awarded Davy Medal in 1880 but **never won the Nobel Prize**.
 
 
 
• **John Dalton** was an English chemist, physicist, and meteorologist. He is infamous for** introducing atomic theory into chemistry**.
 
 
• He also did research work on color blindness. Color blindness is known as **Daltonism** in some countries.
 
• He also **never won the Nobel Prize.**
